analysis.title: The AI Trap
key_insights: The AI trade has moved from crowded to crushed. Positioning is resetting toward extremes, with semiconductor allocations near year lows and NVDA at its most oversold level since 2019.

Goldman notes S&P futures open interest rose $19.1B on November 5, the fifth-largest daily increase in two years excluding rolls, as investors added shorts. Open interest then fell $16.6B as the S&P recovered 2.7% through November 9.
The Market Ear reads much of the rebound as short covering rather than fresh buying.
Goldman argues semiconductors may matter more for the S&P than real yields. On November 5, semis fell 12.2% and the S&P fell 4.4%.
Goldman highlights a negative correlation between asset-manager S&P shorts and semiconductor performance. Without a sustained semis recovery, the broader equity rebound stays vulnerable.
BTIG says heavy volume traded above $165 in SOXX leaves buyers from May to early November underwater. The 200-day MA is near $160, making $160-165 the key zone.
BTIG is bearish below $165 and sees rallies as chances to cut exposure. It sees a possible full retracement to the April breakout zone near $115-120.

Texas holds over a quarter of planned US data center capacity additions through 2030, and talk of a moratorium has hit AI stocks. Goldman says permit limits do not stop projects already under construction.
Goldman says the 35 GW of data center additions planned for 2027 are largely already being built, with limited execution risk. It still sees $1.3T of AI infrastructure capex by 2027.
SOX has had one of its most extreme drawdowns in history. It bounced off its long-term trendline but is well below the 200-day MA.

NVDA is further below its 200-day MA than at any time since Liberation Day, with make-or-break levels near $160. Weekly RSI is below the Liberation Day lows, and the stock is down about 30% from its all-time high.

JPM's aggregate Asian equity positioning indicator is at the 8th percentile, a level that has historically coincided with important market bottoms. Asian equities fell about 15% in a month and tech RSI readings are in the low 20s.
Goldman says Korean semiconductor valuations are back near levels rarely seen in modern market history, including SK Hynix. The market is pricing a structural earnings downturn.
Gold is held between $4,000 and a downward-sloping trendline. The bounce did not reach the 50-day MA, and today is shaping up as the biggest down day since the latest squeeze higher.

market_movers.rationale: The stock is furthest below its 200-day MA since Liberation Day and most oversold since 2019. Make-or-break levels sit near $160.

sector_views.rationale: BTIG is bearish below $165 on SOXX and sees a possible retracement to $115-120. Goldman says semis' fate matters more for the S&P than real yields, and positioning is washed out.
Goldman says the Texas moratorium fears overlook projects already under construction, and it still sees $1.3T of AI capex by 2027. Technical damage remains severe.

earnings_insights: Goldman says Korean semiconductor valuations are depressed because the market is pricing a structural earnings downturn. The note says that if earnings hold up, the valuation gap could become hard to ignore.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Semis fell 12.2% the same day and overwhelmed the hyperscaler complex.
Goldman and The Market Ear attribute much of it to short covering.
Goldman's estimate. It supports the view that the buildout continues despite the selloff.
Gold is trapped between this level and a downward-sloping trendline, and direction is unclear.
